text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Monday.

LONDON - UK blue chips climbed to a record high on Monday as Friday's surge on Wall Street rippled over the Atlantic, boosting investor confidence here, traders said. The FTSE 100 settled 6.7 up at 4,031.5 points. But profit-taking in gilts, T-bonds and in U.S. stocks knocked the index off the day's earlier high of 4,046.8.

FRANKFURT- German shares ended bourse trade on Monday at a new record high above 2,700 points after floor trade caught up with gains made in IBIS electronic trade on Friday on the back of Wall Street strength. The DAX index of 30 blue chip shares opened floor trade above 2,700 points and touched a new record high at 2,704.74 before closing at 2702.64, a gain of 19.36 points. In post-bourse trade the index stood at 2,705.21 up 0.96.

PARIS - French shares closed fractionally lower on Wall Street turning initial gains into small losses, after having spent the day in a very narrow trading range. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 1.14 points or 0.05 percent at 2,151.55.

ZURICH - Swiss shares shrugged off morning doldrums to gain power in the afternoon on Monday and close above the prior record of 3,813.6 points on the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) set in July. Dealers said the index surged due to buying in shares with a heavy SMI weighting. The All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) closed up 8.14 points, or 0.33 percent, at 2,440.05.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed mixed on Monday after moving in narrow ranges and languishing at weaker levels for most of the day, shrugging off a surge on Wall Street. Participants retreated to the sidelines ahead of the long-awaited listing of West Japan Railway Co, brokers said. The key 225-share Nikkei 225 average closed up 12.98 points at 21,161.01.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks staged a powerful advance on Monday, with the Hang Seng index registering its biggest point gain since March, as new records on Wall Street and strong interest in China shares kept buyers active. The Hang Seng rose 227.56 points to close at 12,133.07.

SYDNEY - The Australian stock market, inspired by record highs on Wall Street, closed on Monday within striking distance of the record high of 2350.1 reached on February 3, 1994 despite a holiday in Sydney. The All Ordinaries index closed up 24.3 points at 2339.8, just off its intra-day high of 2341.1, its highest level this year.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares got a late shot in the arm from a strong Wall Street to give life to a market that on Monday was still suffering a hangover from disappointing reserve figures, dealers said on Monday. The overall index finished at 7,036.3, up 15.7 points, as the industrials pulled ahead by 23.3 points to end at 8,245.7. Golds fell 5.9 points to 1,727 as concerns over the weakening bullion price dogged the index.
